title: Structured output robustness harness for quantized function-call responses (FP8 / INT8)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated robustness harness and calibration workflow that measures JSON-schema adherence and function-call fidelity when models are served under FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. The goal is to produce per-field failure rates, confidence-adjusted acceptance thresholds, and a deterministic regression suite that flags quality regressions introduced by quantization or calibration changes.
background: Previous ad-hoc checks showed increased structured-output violations after INT8 calibration on nested arrays and edge-case numerics. Existing tickets focused on calibration schema checks but did not standardize a repeatable dataset, seedable prompts, or per-field tolerance metrics for function-calling outputs. We need a single-source-of-truth harness to compare quant profiles and guide calibration/quant decisions.
approach: Create a canonical prompt corpus (~1.2k prompts) covering: edge-case numerics, nested arrays, optional fields, missing keys, variant ordering, streaming/chunked responses, and aggressive token truncation scenarios.

Implement a schema-aware perturbation stage that mutates correct outputs to generate near-boundary cases (e.g., floats as strings, null vs empty list, truncated JSON fragments) to stress parser resilience.
Run baseline (FP16) and quantized profiles (FP8 dynamic, FP8 static, INT8-per-channel) with identical seeds and batching configs to isolate quantization impact.
Collect structured metrics: schema_validation_failure_rate, field_level_error_rate, missing_key_rate, extra_key_rate, value_type_mismatch_rate, and function_call_misrouting_rate.
Add confidence-calibrated pass/fail using token-level logprob heuristics and per-field entropy thresholds derived from baseline distribution.
Integrate harness into CI: nightly runs, PR gate for quant-related changes, and alerting if schema_failure_rate delta > 0.5% or any high-impact field regression observed.
Document recommended calibration adjustments (per-layer calibration dataset size, clip thresholds) tied to observed failure modes and provide actionable runbook steps.
Ship a comparison dashboard with diff views between profiles and an exportable CSV summarizing per-field deltas.
Collaborate with DX/Console teams to add a per-route structured-output health metric in Console (follow-up ticket).
test_plan: Synthetic corpus generation: seed=42, 1.2k prompts split 70/20/10 for training/calibration/validation.
Calibration workflow: run calibration tune for INT8 with 2k calibration samples, FP8 static profile using mixed-precision fallback, and record weight/activation histograms.
Execution matrix: FP16 baseline, FP8-dyn, FP8-static, INT8-per-channel, INT8-per-tensor (where supported), both with KV-cache enabled and disabled.

Metrics collection: schema_validator (ajv-based) returning pass/fail + path-level error messages, function_call_router correctness (expected function name + args schema), and post-process normalization error counts.
Determinism checks: repeat runs (n=5) confirm variance < 0.2% for non-quantized baseline; quantify variance introduced by quant profiles.
Failure-mode classification: parse errors vs semantic mismatches vs truncated JSON. Each failure assigned severity: low/medium/high.
Regression thresholds: nightly alerts when overall schema_failure_rate increases by >0.5% vs baseline, or when any high-severity failure appears in >0.1% of samples.
Manual spot-check: sample 100 failed items and verify if failure is acceptable (e.g., optional fields) or actionable (e.g., type change causing downstream crash).
acceptance_criteria: Harness implemented and runnable via rwi-quant-harness CLI with a single command and documented flags.
Nightly CI job submits results to the quantization dashboard and stores raw artifacts in s3://redwood-quantation/harness/2026-03.
Baseline FP16 and at least FP8-dyn and INT8-per-channel profiles tested; CSV export contains per-field deltas and aggregated schema_failure_rate.
PR gate added: any change to quant calibration code or serving kernel that modifies schema_failure_rate by >0.5% must include a regression justification and mitigation plan.

Playbook created: recommended calibration parameter adjustments mapped to observed failure patterns (e.g., increase calibration samples for embedding-dense layers, enable per-channel scaling for INT8 on attention weights).

observations: INT8-per-channel reduces memory and is cheaper but correlates with missing closing-brace truncations when tokenization spans quantization-sensitive layers.
FP8-static shows a small increase in type coercion cases where numeric fidelity near large integers flips to scientific notation causing schema failure in strict integer fields.
Streaming mode increases occurrence of truncated JSON fragments; enabling prefix/KV cache reduces truncation rate by ~30% in early tests.
Per-field entropy thresholding reduces false positives by 18% compared to raw schema-only gating, by allowing high-entropy fields (free-text) to be treated leniently.
Calibration dataset diversity matters: calibration that omitted short-tail prompts under-specified activation ranges and increased INT8 failures on short JSON outputs.
decision: Proceed with harness and CI gating. Prioritize fixing INT8-per-tensor path and add calibration dataset augmentation for short outputs. Do not block FP8 rollout but require follow-up mitigations for numeric coercion failures.
remaining_tasks: Hook harness into nightly CI and validate notifications to SRE/QA channels.
Add Console metric mapping for structured-output health and expose top-5 failing fields per route.
Open follow-up ENG tickets for specific kernel/quant fixes identified by failing patterns.
Run cross-region tests (us-west, eu-central) to confirm no extra variance due to hardware differences.
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to run the harness on two enterprise customer corpora under NDA to validate real-world impact.
notes: Keep raw model logits and token-level probabilities for at least 14 days to enable retroactive debugging of failures.
When reporting failures, include hashed prompt id, seed, model_hash, batch_size, kv_cache_state, and quant_profile to allow precise repro.
Avoid suppressing high-severity schema failures via normalization; instead classify and route to mitigation runbook.
